fragments.title: The Speech
fragments.content: I stood before the guests, my voice trembling slightly as I began my speech. I spoke of the past, of old friends and cherished traditions. But beneath the words, I felt a strange emptiness, as if I were performing rather than speaking from the heart.

sensoryDetails.visual: The soft glow of gas lamps on polished silver
sensoryDetails.auditory: The murmur of voices, the rustle of silk dresses
sensoryDetails.tactile: The coldness of the champagne flute in my hand

fragments.title: Gretta's Distraction
fragments.content: I noticed Gretta standing by the window, listening to the song. There was a look on her face I had never seen before - a look of such deep longing that it frightened me. I called her name, but she did not hear. In that moment, I realized I did not know the woman I had married.

sensoryDetails.visual: Gretta's silhouette against the dark window
sensoryDetails.auditory: The faint strains of 'The Lass of Aughrim'
sensoryDetails.tactile: The chill of realization creeping over me

fragments.title: The Epiphany
fragments.content: As I watched the snow falling outside, I understood. All my life I had been living in a dream, blind to the reality of those around me. Gretta had loved another, and that love had been greater than anything I could offer. The dead were not truly dead - they lived on in the memories of the living.

sensoryDetails.visual: Snowflakes falling silently in the moonlight
sensoryDetails.auditory: The distant music from the party fading
sensoryDetails.tactile: The cold glass against my forehead

fragments.title: The Song
fragments.content: The song drifted across the room, and suddenly I was back in Galway, standing in the rain, waiting for Michael. I could feel the cold, hear his voice calling my name. The years fell away, and for a moment, he was there again - young, vibrant, full of love.

sensoryDetails.visual: Michael's face, pale in the moonlight
sensoryDetails.auditory: His voice, clear and strong, singing my song
sensoryDetails.tactile: The cold rain soaking through my shawl

fragments.title: The Confession
fragments.content: I told Gabriel about Michael - how we met, how he loved me, how he died. The words poured out, years of silence finally broken. I did not care if it hurt him; I needed him to know. He deserved the truth, even if it shattered his world.

sensoryDetails.auditory: My own voice, trembling with years of grief
sensoryDetails.tactile: The warmth of the bed contrasting with the coldness in my heart

fragments.title: The Promise
fragments.content: I waited for her in the snow, my coat thin against the winter cold. I had to see her, to tell her how much I loved her. Even as the frost bit into my bones, I could not leave. She was worth every shiver, every breath.

sensoryDetails.visual: The white blanket of snow covering everything
sensoryDetails.auditory: The wind howling through the empty streets
sensoryDetails.tactile: The freezing cold seeping into my very soul

fragments.title: The Last Thought
fragments.content: As the darkness closed in, I thought only of her - her smile, her laugh, the way she said my name. I did not regret what I had done. Love is not measured in years, but in moments. And in that moment, I was truly alive.

sensoryDetails.visual: A flash of Gretta's face in the darkness
sensoryDetails.tactile: The gentle warmth of memory replacing the cold

fragments.title: The Party
fragments.content: I watched the guests dancing, their laughter filling the room. How many years had we hosted this party? Forty, perhaps more. The faces changed, but the joy remained. In these moments, the past and present merged, and for a while, time stood still.

sensoryDetails.auditory: The piano playing a lively tune
sensoryDetails.tactile: The warmth of the fire on my old hands

fragments.title: The Preparation
fragments.content: The house was spotless, the food was ready, the guests would arrive soon. Julia would worry about the details, but I had everything under control. This party was more than just a gathering - it was a thread connecting us to those who had gone before.

sensoryDetails.visual: Tables set with fine china and crystal
sensoryDetails.auditory: The clink of glasses being polished
sensoryDetails.tactile: The smooth linen tablecloth beneath my fingers
